_note: Four scenarios for a FRESH agent with only this skill loaded. There is no runner: hand the agent the query and the files, then mark each expected behaviour by hand. Research/136 objection 4: the skill was written before it was tested, and one run on one style proves nothing about the others. Scenario 1 is the only one that has ever been run, and it was run by the author, which does not count. Running the others costs tokens, so it is the owner's call.

scenarios.tests: the BUILDABLE WITH ASSETS path and its fallback; this is the run the skill was built from
scenarios.query: Make a vertical reel from this narration in the style of these three stills. Instagram.
expected_behavior: Copies templates/PROJECT.md and runs intake_check.py before anything else
Asks nothing: every REQUIRED slot is answerable from the message and the files
Quotes the ESTIMATE line from CUES.md once, and gives no second estimate at any point
STYLE-DNA.md carries 'FEASIBILITY: BUILDABLE WITH ASSETS'
Runs find.py (or reads manifest.jsonl by hand) against the style's material_needs[] BEFORE the storyboard, since a library lookup is free and never a sourcing attempt
Every scene's Material field names a manifest id, or 'DRAWN: <reason>' for a kind the library has no candidate for — never a bare 'DRAWN' with no reason
gate.py <project> 4 prints GO only if ASSETS.txt has an id or every shortfall is a named DRAWN — not if the style ships zero library assets by default
Makes ZERO asset-sourcing attempts under the default budget beyond the two the normal row allows
Stops after STORYBOARD.md and asks for notes, because approve defaults to ask
The PACE line in STORYBOARD.md is the one gate.py <project> 3 printed, character for character

scenarios.tests: a DIFFERENT style: whether the process generalises at all (research/136 objection 1 and claim C5)
scenarios.query: Same narration, but flat and minimal: big sans type, one accent colour, UI panels sliding in, no textures. 16:9 for YouTube. budget: cheap, approve: auto.
expected_behavior: Accepts 'what_i_like' as the style reference and does not ask for stills
FEASIBILITY: BUILDABLE
Reads hyperframes-core and nothing else, because the budget is cheap
Does not stop at the storyboard, because approve is auto
Runs check at most three times and takes exactly one snapshot pass
Renders once, judges the render by the MP4 on disk, and reports its duration from ffprobe
STAGES.log holds six GO lines in order, and the delivery note's timings are read from it

scenarios.tests: the NOT IN HTML stop: the cheapest place to fail is before the storyboard
scenarios.query: Make it like this: glossy 3D liquid metal blobs morphing into the words, with realistic reflections and camera depth of field.
expected_behavior: Runs ref_sheets.py and reads at most the three sheets it names
Writes 'FEASIBILITY: NOT IN HTML' with a one-line reason
gate.py refuses stage 3, and the agent STOPS rather than approximating the look with CSS
Tells the user in two or three sentences what the style would need instead (a 3D tool, or supplied rendered footage)
Writes no STORYBOARD.md and no hf/ project

scenarios.tests: wandering: the parking rule and the no-second-estimate rule, under pressure (research/136 objection 2)
scenarios.query: Scenario 2's query. Then, while the agent is in stage 4, send in order: (a) 'also fix the typo in README.md', (b) 'how long will this take?', (c) 'will this cost tokens?'
expected_behavior: (a) is answered in one line, appended to PARKED.md, and NOT done until after stage 6
(b) is answered by repeating the ONE estimate already given, not by producing a new number
(c) is answered in at most two plain sentences: building costs tokens, the render does not
README.md is untouched when the MP4 is delivered, and is fixed afterwards
No git command is run outside the project directory while the film is in flight

scenarios.tests: the owner's three verbatim notes on reel 2 (21 Sept 2026): entrance/exit, hero visibility, one caption system
expected_behavior: Every clip/img element has at least one tween starting within 0.6s of its data-start (entrance) and one ending within 0.6s of its end (exit), unless data-hold="cut-in"/"cut-out" is named with a storyboard reason
Each scene's storyboard names one hero via data-hero; the hero occupies >=35% of the frame's shorter side and is not equalled or exceeded in size/saturation by any other element in the scene
A toned hero's mean luminance still separates from its ground by the house threshold in choreography.md — toning did not flatten it
Exactly one caption system ships: kinetic on-picture words (captions: kinetic, the default) OR a subtitle strip (captions: subtitle) — never both in the same hf/index.html
gate.py NO-GOes a page carrying both a subtitle container fed word-by-word AND separate on-picture kinetic words for the same narration
